author: Dhiraj Sharma
content: I recently worked on an Android app that communicates with a smart device via Bluetooth. The challenge was that the device itself wasn’t physically available locally, making normal app debugging impossible. To solve this, I set up a remote debugging workflow using Termux on an remote Android device, reverse SSH tunneling, and ADB over TCP/IP. This allowed me to connect to the remote device indirectly, test and debug the app in real time, without shipping hardware or relying on paid tunneling services. The full setup and helper scripts are documented here: https://lnkd.in/gE4YUMBF It’s a practical approach for anyone dealing with IoT, embedded devices, or apps that need to be tested remotely. hashtag #RemoteDebugging hashtag #AndroidDevelopment hashtag #IoT hashtag #FirmwareTesting hashtag #ADB hashtag #Termux hashtag #AutomationTools
